title: A Look at the Wider Divide in Credit Card Delinquency by Income - Liberty Street Economics
gist: NY Fed researchers show US credit card serious-delinquency flows have risen above pre-pandemic levels for all income groups since 2022, with the low- vs high-income zip-code gap widening. Beyond exhausted savings and inflation outpacing low-income wages, they trace part of the stress to pandemic-era underwriting easing (median origination score fell 699 to 688; low-income share of new cards up ~2pp), and expect delinquencies to keep improving absent macro shocks as the weak 2020-22 vintage fades.

insights.claim: Since 2022, the flow of US credit card balances into serious (90+ day) delinquency has risen above pre-pandemic levels for every zip-code income quartile, per the NY Fed Consumer Credit Panel/Equifax.
insights.speaker: Donghoon Lee
entities: New York Fed Consumer Credit Panel
